counterfactual_missing_items: no clear evidence of trauma or infection
no signs of Cushing syndrome or endocrinopathy
decisive_items: a posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7, with a maximum thickness of 10 mm that was homogeneously hyperintense on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted sequences, suggestive of fat
ascending spastic weakness of the lower limbs
graded sensory loss below the D10 level
response.rationale: R1 is the most likely diagnosis due to the presence of a posterior epidural mass suggestive of fat, which is consistent with spinal epidural lipomatosis. R3 is a close runner-up, but the symptoms of ascending spastic weakness and sensory loss can be explained by the epidural mass causing spinal cord compression, which is a consequence of the underlying condition, spinal epidural lipomatosis.

rejected.why: C1 is an append-only completion of R3 and does not provide a distinct diagnosis.
